To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
extracellular copper modifies the resting membrane potential, the input resistance and the firing rate of nodose ganglia neurons.
copper modulates the activity in a subpopulation of nodose ganglia neurons in vitro.
micromolar copper modifies the electrical properties of nodose ganglia neurons in vitro, increasing the excitatory state of most of the neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the modulation of neuronal excitability and synaptic transmission in the peripheral nervous system.
the effects of extracellular copper on peripheral neurons.
the study of the effects of copper on the electrical activity and the membrane properties of peripheral neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu2+ ions modify the activity of peripheral sensory neurons, increasing the neuronal excitability and spontaneous discharges.
copper modifies the membrane properties of nodose ganglia neurons in a way that increases the excitability of the neurons.
copper modulates the electrical activity of peripheral neurons and this effect may be related with copper’s role in peripheral sensory pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the copper modifies the electrical properties and spontaneous firing activity of the peripheral neurons.
Cu2+ modifies electrical membrane properties of nodose ganglia neurons in a redox-independent fashion and that this effect may be mediated by a modulation of the voltage-gated calcium channels.

copper modulates the electrical properties of the neurons of the peripheral nervous system and that the nodose ganglia preparation in vitro can be used as an experimental model for studying the effects of this metal on neuronal activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of Cu2+ on the electrical activity of the peripheral neuron may be mediated by changes in the resting membrane potential, the input resistance and/or the voltage-gated sodium channels.
copper may play an important role in the modulation of peripheral neuronal activity.
copper can modify the activity of peripheral ganglion neurons, which may contribute to the modulation of the sensory information reaching the central nervous system.
